records.text: Hillary Clinton sought the location of Gilgamesh's tomb a few days before the United States invaded Iraq.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Do you guys ever wonder why Hillary Clinton in those WikiLeak emails was asking a few days before we invaded Iraq, she was trying to locate Gilgamesh's tomb.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The email about locating Gilgamesh's tomb was a 2018 Freedom of Information Act request sent to the State Department by requester Denetra Senigar; it was not a directive or search request from Hillary Clinton. It also came fifteen years after the 2003 invasion of Iraq, not shortly before it.

sources.title: Lead Stories: Hillary Clinton and the Gilgamesh FOIA email
sources.relevance: Identifies the document as a private citizen's 2018 FOIA request and directly contradicts both the attribution to Clinton and the pre-invasion timing.

records.text: They did find Gilgamesh, aka Nimrod.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep QRS_hR7NXaQ)

appearances.snippet: You need to look up the research that was done by Rob Skiba. They did find Gilgamesh, aka Nimrod.

verification.notes: Transcript context identifies the asserted equation of Gilgamesh with Nimrod. Current scholarship treats Nimrod's historical identity as uncertain and does not identify him as Gilgamesh; the claim that archaeologists found Gilgamesh, also known as Nimrod, is unsupported and false as stated.

sources.title: Nimrod, Mighty Hunter and King - Who Was He?
sources.relevance: Scholarly review explains that Nimrod's identity is unresolved and does not establish Gilgamesh as Nimrod.

records.text: We invaded just after Gilgamesh was found.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep QRS_hR7NXaQ)

appearances.snippet: Yes, we invaded just after he was found.

verification.notes: Transcript places the alleged discovery immediately before the 2003 invasion. A BBC report dated April 29, 2003 described a possible tomb match, after the March invasion began, while the underlying geophysical fieldwork occurred before the war. The chronology and certainty in the statement are therefore materially misleading.

sources.title: Gilgamesh tomb believed found
sources.relevance: April 29, 2003 report postdates the invasion and records only a tentative identification.

sources.title: Uruk - City of Gilgamesh: First tests in 2001 for magnetic prospecting
sources.relevance: Primary research paper establishes that the underlying prospecting began in 2001.

records.text: The first place that U.S. forces went during the Iraq War and set up a base was a museum that held relics, Babylonian cuneiform tablets, and Gilgamesh's tomb.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep QRS_hR7NXaQ)

appearances.snippet: The first place that we went during that war and set up a base was a museum. Not just any museum, the museum that held all of the relics. licks for that. It also held all the cuneiform tablets from Babylon and Gilgamesh and or Nimrod's tomb.

verification.notes: Transcript asserts that the museum/relic site was the first destination and base of U.S. forces. Current institutional records show Camp Alpha was established at Babylon after the invasion, but do not show it was the first place U.S. forces went; the Gilgamesh work was at Uruk, a different site. The composite claim is false.

sources.title: Report on Damage Assessments in Babylon
sources.relevance: UNESCO documents the later military base at Babylon but does not support the first-destination allegation.

sources.title: German Archaeological Institute - Uruk (Warka)
sources.relevance: Official project page locates the Gilgamesh-related prospecting at Uruk, not the Babylon museum/base.

records.text: The German geophysicists became convinced between May 2002 and very early 2003 that they had found Gilgamesh's tomb.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: When exactly did they find it? We know for sure that it was sometime between May 2002 and very early 2003. They became convinced that indeed they had found the actual tomb of Gilgamesh,

verification.notes: Transcript claims the team was convinced it had found Gilgamesh's tomb by early 2003. The April 2003 BBC report quotes Jorg Fassbinder expressly declining a definite identification and saying only that the layout looked similar to the epic. The claim overstates both certainty and discovery.

sources.title: Gilgamesh tomb believed found
sources.relevance: Fassbinder explicitly declines a definite identification and describes only similarity to the epic.

records.text: The BBC reported that Jorg Fassbinder had discovered Gilgamesh's tomb.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: The public is informed a couple of weeks thereafter, the BBC, so state arm, that Fassbinder indeed had made the discovery of Gilgamesh's tomb.

verification.notes: The BBC did report on April 29, 2003 that a German-led team believed it may have located a tomb matching the Epic of Gilgamesh. However, Fassbinder explicitly said he would not identify it definitively. Reporting existed, but 'discovered the tomb' overstates the article.

sources.title: Gilgamesh tomb believed found
sources.relevance: Confirms the BBC report while showing the discovery language was tentative.

records.text: A State Department FOIA request sought documents about the resurrection chamber of Gilgamesh, the location of his body, and the location of buried Nephilim.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: there was this still never quite explained FOIA request that went through the State Department requesting documents pertaining to the resurrection chamber of Gilgamesh, the location of his body and the location of the buried Nephilim.

verification.notes: Transcript refers to the existence and wording of a State Department FOIA request. The department's official FOIA log contains a private request seeking documents about a Gilgamesh resurrection chamber, his body, and buried Nephilim. This verifies the request only, not the existence of responsive records or the underlying claims.

sources.title: U.S. Department of State FOIA Log AC-2023-00002
sources.relevance: Official log contains the private request and its Gilgamesh, resurrection chamber, body, and Nephilim wording.

records.text: The United States extracted Gilgamesh's tomb roughly two years after invading Iraq in 2003.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Okay. So we invaded, as I mentioned yesterday, mid 2003, and we extracted Gilgamesh, Gilgamesh's tomb roughly two years later.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. Contemporary archaeology reporting described geophysical evidence of structures that might correspond to a grave, not an excavated tomb or body. The German Archaeological Institute says war interrupted the work and large areas remained unexcavated; no credible evidence supports a later U.S. extraction.

sources.title: German Archaeological Institute — Research Projects of the Orient Department
sources.relevance: Says work at Uruk was interrupted in 2003 and large portions remained unexcavated.

sources.title: Fact Check: Video Does NOT Show Treasures Looted From Tomb Of Gilgamesh
sources.relevance: Explains the 2003 find was possible subsurface structures, not an excavated tomb or body.

records.text: Gilgamesh's body was found in the Iraqi desert in 2003.
records.speaker: Rob Skiba

appearances.snippet: 2003, the body of Gilgamesh was found in the desert of Iraq.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. The 2003 Uruk story concerned magnetometer-detected structures that an archaeologist cautiously said might resemble the epic description; no Gilgamesh body was found or excavated. Later viral body and mummy claims have been specifically debunked.

sources.title: Fact Check: Video Does NOT Show Treasures Looted From Tomb Of Gilgamesh
sources.relevance: Explains no Gilgamesh body was found in the 2003 Uruk survey.

records.text: A special operations general said Gilgamesh's remains were in a remarkable state of preservation and that 'they' had the remains.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep DYD_QHMPwqM)

appearances.snippet: I talked to a special operations general who validated that, and his words were he was in a state of remarkable preservation, okay? He said they have Gilgamesh's remains.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. The statement relies on an unnamed alleged special-operations general, and searches found no authenticated interview, military record, excavation record, or independent corroboration that Gilgamesh remains were recovered and held. The hearsay cannot be verified.

conveyance.original_source: Conversation recounted on Omega Man Radio

records.text: The U.S. military occupation phase of Iraq began one month after Gilgamesh's body was found.
records.speaker: Rob Skiba

appearances.snippet: Interesting that the U.S. military started its military occupation phase of Iraq one month later.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. No Gilgamesh body was found in 2003; reporting described only possible subsurface structures. U.S. invasion and occupation activity began before and during that archaeological reporting, so the claimed one-month-after-body chronology is false.

sources.title: Fact Check: Video Does NOT Show Treasures Looted From Tomb Of Gilgamesh
sources.relevance: Refutes the premise that a Gilgamesh body was found before the alleged occupation chronology.

sources.title: Learning from Our Military History: The United States Army, Operation Iraqi Freedom, and the Potential for Operational Art and Thinking
sources.relevance: Provides the official March-May 2003 invasion and occupation chronology.
